The past still shines across the years,
But cannot make them new;
It is distinct, it is remote,
And cold because it’s true.

Food is not a stair to heaven,
Nor proof that thought is done;
It is the body’s daily word,
The work of flesh and sun.
We eat, we question, we begin,
We gather and divide;
The meal becomes a common table
Where every doubt can sit.

Has my heart gone quiet?
Have the dream-bees left their hive?
Is the wheel of thought stopped,
With no water left to drive?
No—the heart is awake,
Wide open in the dark;
It watches distant signals,
And waits for one small spark.

Summer arrives, then winter wins;
The daisies lose their place.
But when the southern wind returns,
The frost forgets its face.
It pours a softer song through fields,
It loosens every stone;
The season that was conquered once
Comes asking for its own.

When I was young, I swore my heart
Would never leave its room;
No private thought would meet the air,
No secret face the sun.
Then love came like a public wind,
And opened every door;
It carried what I meant to hide
Across the world once more.

I read a rare truth in the news:
No evidence was found.
The politician smiled and said,
“Then surely I am sound.”
But someone asked, “How hard did they
Look underneath the floor?”
The headline closed; the question stayed,
And troubled us much more.

I woke from a dream where you smiled,
A princess among the flowers;
The garden shone, the spring ran high,
The world belonged to ours.
You kissed the frog beside the pond—
I laughed because I knew:
The prince was not the creature there;
The frog was me, with you.

Cross the line and leave the room
Where smaller dreams are kept;
Unfasten both your folded wings,
Go where the horizon steps.
The world is more than what you know,
The sky is more than blue;
Freedom begins the moment you
Decide to follow through.

Green waves move through the cornfield,
And roses mark the lane;
The morning wore a summer crown,
The evening wears the rain.
The green has turned to amber now,
The paths are full of cold;
I grow older with the field,
And feel the year unfold.

Grandfather stands in afternoon light,
His wrinkles full of sun;
He laughs, and Grandma hides her smile,
Though she is laughing too.
Their stories cross the kitchen,
Their eyes begin to shine;
The water in their laughter is
A family’s oldest wine.

“Would you like a drink?” she asked.
“Yes—though I’m not quite sure.”
“No charge,” she said, and passed it on.
Then asked, “Do you like blue?”
I paused; she laughed and chose for me.
The room became a view:
Some questions ask for honest thought,
Some only ask for thanks.

Do not disturb me, friend;
The hooded crows are singing.
Their rough black music fills the noon,
And all the light is ringing.
I would rather hear their honest calls
Than listen to a tongue
That turns a sunny day to blame
Before the day is done.

Come sit beside me, lonely ones;
The moon is cold tonight.
The streets have lost their footsteps,
The windows hide their light.
Winter has begun to gather stars
Above the sleeping snow;
If you are lonely, speak to me—
I have nowhere else to go.

I took a rose from the garden,
An orange bloom from the wall;
I mixed them with speedwell,
With apple blossoms small.
Their colors and scents together
Made one name sweet and bright,
A lady’s name in petals
That vanished by the night.

Outside, the weather hardens;
The frost has sealed the street.
Inside these old stone walls,
The cold comes to eat.
It settles in the rafters,
It waits beside the fire;
The house keeps one thin warmth
Against the winter’s wire.

My son is sleeping,
One long leg across the bed;
His hands are broad upon the quilt,
His childhood almost fled.
Not quite a boy, not yet a man,
He fills the room with grace;
I watch the years become a child
Before my watching face.

Invisible identity,
Endless forms beneath the skin;
Life reveals itself in motion,
Outward shape and inward change.
Measure what you can, but know
The deepest force is hidden;
Power moves beyond the eye,
Beyond the world’s accounting.

This is my letter to the world,
Though no one wrote to me:
The meadow spoke in quiet green,
The river answered free.
I leave these words in unseen hands,
Among the leaves and air;
If I have loved the living earth,
Then read them gently there.

Summer passes through the glass,
And roses lose their red;
The days continue one by one,
Though nothing stays as said.
We hold the bloom, we name the love,
We watch the hours go;
The flower’s beauty teaches us
How quickly beauty goes.

I thought my Thanksgiving lost
When my gray cat disappeared;
Then he came home before the night,
And every fear cleared.
I give thanks for health and kin,
For grace, for food, for that;
And for the heavy, purring proof
That came home like a cat.

What love has joined is not undone
By ceremony’s thread;
The heart knows whom it chose to keep,
And whom it left instead.
Marriage may be vows and rings,
Or words the priests repeat;
But love can brush the page aside
And make its own decree.

Dance, little child, above the floor;
Your mother’s arms are near.
Clap your hands and turn around,
There is no room for fear.
Up toward the ceiling, down again,
Backward, forward, round;
Your laughter is the little bell
That makes the whole house sound.

I am no star of perfect form;
The world has brighter faces.
But I can live behind my own,
And let it make its faces.
If beauty stands before the glass,
I need not take the blame;
The people looking back at me
Are the ones who choose the frame.

I am a bridge of colored stone,
With grief beneath my feet;
The river carries pain below,
The valley smells of sweet.
Screwpine flowers line the banks,
Bright invitations there;
I wait for those who cross the span
To stop and breathe the air.

You are uncertain, bright, and brave,
A clever shark at sea;
You smile at someone’s empty heart,
Then hunt him quietly.
Your teeth make shadows in the night,
Your charm disguises fear;
He loves you though you circle him—
Deceit is swimming near.

In failure and in victory,
Keep your mind at rest;
Do the work that falls to you,
And offer it your best.
Do not mistake the seed for fruit,
Or claim what time must bear;
The hand that works without demand
Is lighter in the air.

Water is clear,
Water is kind,
Water can carry
Body and mind.
It falls without price,
It waits in the sea;
The lives that we live
Depend on it freely.

My sorrow falls like petals
From a flower no one sees;
The sky has lost its memory,
The snow has lost its ease.
I touch the earth, and feel it break
Like porcelain in rain;
The grief is beautiful and strange,
And beautiful again.

Grandfather money,
Father money,
Mother money too;
Brother money, sister money,
Friends who count it through.
Do not love the coins alone,
Or measure hearts by pay;
Earn what keeps your hands alive,
Then give some love away.

Cold moon, wolf moon, storm moon,
Snow moon in the sky;
The long night spreads its silver cloth,
The winter shadows fly.
The fires burn a little low,
The dark moves through the room;
Still hope remains beneath the ice,
Waiting for the bloom.

Go where no road has been worn smooth;
Cut through the waiting grass.
If your heart must crack to move,
Let it crack, not break.
The path appears beneath the foot
That chooses to advance;
Silence may be loved, but life
Still asks the heart to dance.

He sees her heart in pieces,
Reflected in his eyes;
He hears her grief like distant prayer
Beneath cathedral skies.
He wants to make the old shape whole,
But sorrow will not bend;
Some things are mended slowly,
And some must simply end.

I cannot stay much longer;
The sea has heard me cry.
Pull down the sails, the wind comes limping,
Dark beneath the sky.
It wraps my aching bones in fog,
It teaches me to lie;
I leave the harbor without words,
And let the water decide.

I learned to work at Cascade Dairy,
On the Carter family farm;
Parkdale sat beneath Mount Hood,
Eleven miles by crow’s flight.
The mountain gave the horizon scale,
The pasture gave me time;
That farm was where a poet first
Learned to begin a journey.

Beyond the sea, the mountains form
One unbroken line;
The sky becomes the ground we walk,
The mist another sign.
Leaves arrive, then stones appear,
Each proof becomes unclear;
I come to do a partial thing,
And keep a portion here.

The gold of day has passed away,
The evening turns to blue;
The shepherd’s flute has lost its sound,
The fields have lost their hue.
The same dusk gathers every year,
The same old light departs;
It leaves a quiet in the hills
And silence in our hearts.

The park is bright with flying discs,
With dogs and families;
My parents sit upon a bench,
My father watches me.
He tosses up a baseball high,
Then shows me how to catch;
I reach, I miss, he laughs with me,
And teaches me again.

Change comes,
Change stays,
Change turns the road;
Nothing keeps
Its former load.
Change is not
A passing guest;
Without change,
Nothing grows.

“Nothing golden keeps its place,”
You told me by the stream.
Green replaces every gold,
Yet gold returns in dream.
The summer leaf becomes the flame
That autumn carries through;
What changes color does not die—
It changes into new.

I love the quiet days like this,
When we are close and still;
Together, yet alone enough
To hear the window’s will.
Later I will remember them,
Their simple joy and grace;
The best days leave no monument,
Only warmth in their place.

Wheel-roll!
My heart is an empty cart,
Waiting for the dawn;
Fill it with a road of light,
Carry sorrow on.
Past the hill and past the bend,
Past the fields of stone;
Let the wheels keep turning till
The road becomes my own.

The harvest whitens all the fields,
The sickles flash and sing;
The reapers bring the golden grain
Before the dark can close.
Yet underneath the thankful song,
Some hearts are bent with grief;
The earth gives bread, the earth takes back,
And neither finds relief.

She rests among the ancient stones,
Where grasses cross her name;
The living pass, the old walls shine,
The sunlight stays the same.
Others once laughed across this ground,
But none will follow her;
The grave is not a door to elsewhere,
It is the place made permanent.

You enter my gray weather
With a pocketful of sun;
The shadows turn to golden roads,
The lonely day comes undone.
Stay with me until the end,
Until the light grows thin;
Your warmth can make a world of gold
Where no light once came in.

The sun has gone; the tall grass waves,
The wild bird leaves the stone.
The landscape holds no lamp or voice,
The evening stands alone.
Only the wind comes from the sea,
It sighs across the plain;
I listen for a footstep,
But hear the dark remain.

May this year bring laughter,
And mornings free of gray;
May friends lift up your tired heart
And brighten every day.
May simple things give peace enough,
May sorrow loosen strife;
May joy arrive without a crown
And settle into life.

Across the fields of yesterday,
A boy comes back to me;
His pockets hold a summer stone,
His eyes still want to see.
He smiles, but not without regret,
Then slips into my skin;
I wonder if he came to meet
The man I might have been.

Hope is a bellflower trembling,
Love a rose in June;
Faith is a white lily
That lifts its face to noon.
The rose has thorns, but still it blooms,
And gives the world its art;
Of all the flowers I have known,
It most resembles the heart.

In seventeen-forty-nine,
The devil drew a crooked line;
He meant to make a swine,
But changed his mind in time,
And fashioned Andrew Turner fine.

Tomorrow opens like a door,
Though no one knows the room;
The morning brings an empty page,
The day decides the tune.
Keep your head above the dark,
Let hopeful thoughts be heard;
One life is all the world gives us,
So choose the brighter word.

Before my bed, the moonlight lies
Like frost upon the floor;
I raise my head and watch it shine,
Then lower it once more.
The room becomes a distant road,
The night becomes my home;
In dreams I walk the streets I knew,
And do not walk alone.

The oldest poems outlive their hands,
Their voices cross the years;
The words that once belonged to one
Return through many ears.
The world of letters keeps its light,
Because the mind makes room;
Each reader gives the written page
Another life to bloom.

My car has stopped beside the road;
The future still feels kind.
At least I had the chance to drive,
To leave some miles behind.
It is like love: without the loss,
What comfort could remain?
The broken engine holds a truth—
The past was worth the pain.

A little girl upon her mother’s knee
Sings a pop song bright and wild;
She misses half the words, but still
She owns the room, the child.
Her mother bounces her in time,
The melody goes wrong;
We smile because the sweetest note
Is sometimes not the song.

Happiness is a seed you plant,
Then water every day;
It grows in faces turned toward you,
In hands that choose to stay.
The fruit is not a hidden prize,
It ripens in the giving;
Look around and help it spread—
That is the art of living.

Silence lived inside their house
Until the years overflowed;
Then a child cried in the spring,
And every window glowed.
The clouds shook loose their heavy dark,
The empty rooms grew warm;
Joy arrived in a small voice
And made a home from storm.

Is life like frost upon a leaf,
That falls one drop at a time?
The cold makes every surface shine,
Then leaves before the climb.
Age slips away from branch and hand,
The world continues on;
We cannot keep the shining drop,
But we can see it once.

Animals do not invent excuses—
At least, that is what we say;
We hide our wants behind polite
And complicated play.
The fox may steal, the human schemes,
The wolf may take what’s free;
Perhaps the honest creature is
The one we pretend to be.

We taught across the hallway,
Through seasons of bell and noise;
The restless children entered small,
Then left as women, boys.
We taught them skills and difficult aims,
We watched the shy ones grow;
The colleague loved by everyone
Still walks the halls I know.

At the great cliff of life I stand,
And ask the Lord to guide;
Take my hand through shadowed paths,
Be always at my side.
Lead me where the blessed fields
Open beyond the blue;
Let love be more than fear of death,
And let me walk with You.

There was an Old Woman of Clare,
Who braided moonlight in her hair;
She danced with the mice,
Gave the fairies advice,
And left little stars everywhere.

Power fades,
Wealth departs,
Night follows day,
Dawn leaves the dark.
But one small light
On the hill remains—
A mystery burning
Beyond all names.

Rain moves down the mountain’s face;
The clouds conceal the peak.
They come and go, they change their shape,
They say what words can’t speak.
The mountain keeps its patient green,
Its roots below the weather;
The sky may wander anywhere,
The stone remains together.

In December I avoid June,
The warm places, the names;
The gifts once given without love
Are cardboard, dust, and shame.
Yet one small tear you gave to me
Still has not been thrown away;
I carry it through winter
As proof of another day.

The birds are singing now,
A bright song through the leaves;
I want to thank them one by one
For all the joy it gives.
But night changes every melody,
And silence takes the street;
The same song that seemed like sunlight
Turns distant in the dark.

On summer holiday,
Put down the heavy books;
Go watch the moon above the sea,
Where silver water looks.
Let law and work wait one night,
Let the tide erase the day;
The mind learns more from open sky
Than from a page in shade.

Peace, peace, and peace of mind—
They are not the same.
One may quiet distant streets,
One may still the flame.
We know the words, then lose them,
Forget what they once meant;
The creature searching for them now
Is the one we have become.

The birthday comes with timing strange;
Still, friend, I wish you cheer.
Another year has climbed the hill,
And wisdom waits up here.
Sit down, enjoy the day a while,
Let fate do what it will;
At seventy-six, you’ll find that age
Is growing with you still.

My friend, do not condemn me;
I will not condemn you.
Between the saddle and the earth,
Mercy saw us through.
The ground was hard beneath our feet,
The sky was wide above;
We asked for grace, and grace arrived
Before we asked for love.

Seize the day, the saying cries;
It pulls me by the sleeve.
I race to catch the falling sun,
And scarcely stop to breathe.
What if the day is not a horse?
What if the light can wait?
I run so hard toward living
That I forget to live.

My destiny is not a throne,
Nor fame above the crowd;
It is to live without a mask,
To love without being ashamed.
My destiny is not foretold—
It grows beneath my feet;
Each choice becomes a line of road,
Each breath makes life complete.

Thank you is a little word,
But nothing ranks above it;
It carries kindness back again
To the hands that first had given.
No speech, no gift, no grand parade
Can say what it can do;
The heart speaks plainly when it says,
“I am grateful for you.”

What is freedom?
The open gate?
The right to speak?
The chance to choose?
We take it as a given,
Then use it for ourselves;
Perhaps the first free act would be
To make more room for others.

“Look—a butterfly. Make a wish.”
“I thought wishes were for stars.”
“They are for anything that flies.”
“Does it count if it flies away?”
“Only if you wished before it did.”

For thirty years I studied poems
And tried to speak with care;
Then some curious gentleman
Explained my work to me.
He carried names of distant poets
As though he owned the road;
I kept my mouth shut, smiling,
And let him bear the load.

Trust love when she is difficult;
Trust silence when it’s pure.
Lay down the guarded parts of self
Before the one who knows.
The heart may fail, the body tire,
The stars may lose their way;
But peace can live in faithful hands
When fear has had its day.

Before I had a name or face,
You knew the road I’d take;
Before my father held my hand,
You knew the vows he’d make.
When every earthly thing comes loose,
When all my walls depart,
Your presence stays beneath the ribs,
Still beating in my heart.

Truth can hide beneath a stone,
But it is not erased;
It waits beneath the covering,
Then rises into place.
It is a wound that opens clean,
It is a lamp in rain;
The world may try to silence it,
But truth returns again.

Last night you came to me in dreams,
Your weathered face was bright;
Your eyes were still the deepest blue,
Your hands still held the light.
I folded into memory,
Then woke to an empty room;
The love remained, the dream was gone,
And morning made it true.

For richer, or for richer still,
In status, work, and fame;
For as long as schedules leave
Some room to sign my name.
I take you as my partner now,
With clauses small and neat;
The heart has entered modern life,
Where love must make an appointment.

Like roots beneath one ancient tree,
You steady me below;
When darkness bends the branches down,
Your strength is what I know.
The bark may crack, the storms may come,
The upper leaves may flee;
I stand because you hold the earth
And share its depth with me.

Today is Marathon Day,
And runners cross the screen;
I wonder if the road beyond
Has checkpoints painted clean.
Perhaps the gates of heaven wait
Behind a finish line;
I hope the angels offer water
When I reach the time.

Happiness is strawberries,
Red beneath the rain;
It smells of fruit and summer fields,
Then disappears again.
It tastes of oranges in May,
It shines in rainbow weather;
The sweetest joy is not a thing—
It is the taste together.

The road to success bends hard;
Failure is a turn.
Confusion is the foggy lane,
And enemies make you learn.
Friends can be the speed bumps,
Family the warning light;
Determination is the spare,
Faith keeps the engine right.

I love changing addresses,
Though leaving hurts at first;
The old rooms keep familiar ghosts,
The new ones quench the thirst.
You lose a few old friendships,
Then find new hands to hold;
The map becomes a living thing,
And every move unfolds.

Sometimes the wound must teach the skin,
Sometimes a failure clears the sight;
The tears wash windows of the heart
And let in different light.
We do not understand the road
Until the feet have slipped;
The vision waits behind the pain
That once had closed the eyes.

The internet joins distant hands,
It opens doors to art;
It lets a quiet writer find
Another listening heart.
The village fits within a screen,
The world becomes less wide;
But every tool can build a bridge
Or make a wall inside.

What can I bring you through the dark?
A candle, perhaps, a song?
What can I offer that is true
When everything is wrong?
Look in my eyes; the answer waits
In every word I say:
I cannot mend the broken world,
But I can stay.

Humor opens windows
In rooms where sadness stays;
It teaches tired hearts to move,
It brightens difficult days.
A joke can turn the house around,
Make sorrow miss the door;
Love needs a little laughter
To remain itself once more.

My love is honey gathered slow
From every former spring;
The bees have carried sorrow too,
And made it nourishing.
The past lies folded in the scent,
The present in the thread;
Words weave the two together
Above the tears we shed.

Playwright Eugene O’Neill,
The stage is one grand trick;
The lights rise up, the shadows fall,
The heart performs its act.
I thought I felt a thing called love
Behind the painted scene;
Perhaps the play was all I had,
But it was real to me.

Add one pale blue to two white clouds,
Stir in a little sun;
You’ll find the color of the pools
Where Kuang Si rivers run.
The waterfall leaves the cliff,
Then spreads through shining stone;
Laughter echoes through the spray,
And afternoon lets go.

Fresh fragrance of trust,
Your hand inside of mine;
We walk the road you came to find
When I forgot to call.
The path remembers both our feet,
The quiet knows your name;
Some friendships begin in apology
And never leave the same.

I dreamed you gave me a purple car
And offered me the wheel;
You walked beside it silently,
As though the dream were real.
I drove through roads from childhood,
You watched without a word;
The strangest part of all was that
Your silence could be heard.

Hope has a feathered voice,
It sings beneath the skin;
The storm may shout, the road may fail,
Yet still the song begins.
It asks no bread, it asks no wage,
It simply will not cease;
The smallest bird inside the heart
Can carry us through grief.

Water, water, everywhere—
Cloud, river, rain, and sea;
It shapes the stone, it feeds the root,
It carries you and me.
The smallest drop can hold a sky,
The deepest pool can shine;
Devotion moves like water does,
Outside us and within.

When we grow older, love remains
The youth we cannot lose;
It follows rainbows after rain,
It gives the heart its news.
We may grow slow, we may grow gray,
We may forget the tune;
But love can make the oldest hands
Reach for a younger moon.

If you want your dream to live,
Risk the door and go;
If you wait for perfect proof,
Someone else will know.
The world is full of borrowed plans,
Of lives that never start;
Take the chance before the chance
Is only someone’s art.

My sister Laura lifts me high,
Though I am older, tall;
I tug and strain, but cannot budge
Her from the kitchen wall.
She must have hidden in her shoes
A brick or two inside;
Or perhaps she simply knows
How strength and laughter hide.

The sky keeps watch above her tower,
The moon leans in to hear;
She waits beside the window,
Though no prince has yet come near.
Her castle holds a thousand lights,
Her heart holds one bright hope;
She looks beyond the sleeping road
And trusts the dark to open.

The air sings for you,
The river answers too;
The leaves lift up their voices,
The hills repeat them through.
I stand among the choruses,
Unsure what I should say;
The world is singing all around,
And you are in the way.

I long to find a field untouched,
Where springs remain and flow;
Where lilies open without fear,
And no sharp hailstones fall.
I ask for somewhere past the storm,
Beyond the restless sea;
Some quiet green, some sheltered place,
Where peace can wait for me.

The husband should honor the wife
Whose hands have served the home;
She carries children, elders, work,
And makes the household whole.
Let love be more than gratitude
Spoken when the day is through;
The one who gives the most away
Deserves a life given too.

There was a strange round animal
Who curled up at a call;
One autumn day he rolled so far
He disappeared from all.
They searched beneath the garden gate,
Then heard him shout, “I’m fine!”

Time circles every life,
Then vanishes from view;
It leaves, returns, and leaves again,
As only time can do.
We think we own an afternoon,
Then find the hour has flown;
The clock keeps all its secrets,
And lends us none of its own.

Dark eyes beneath dark hair,
A face the room could not ignore;
She crossed the space in two small steps,
And my heart crossed the floor.
Beauty is a sudden thing,
It does not ask permission;
One glance can turn the ordinary
Into a new condition.

The wind worries the shingles,
The pier groans in the cold;
The sea counts every stone below,
Its silver story told.
I wrap my coat around your arm,
Though fear comes down like rain;
Love is the ache that holds us close
When darkness fills the plain.

My little son plays football,
His feet are still unsure;
He runs as though the ball were wild,
Then scores a goal by chance.
His teammates cheer, the parents laugh,
The league becomes a dream;
No polished player I have seen
Has made me prouder yet.

Greed is dark and one-eyed;
It swells, then loses air.
It gathers every shining thing,
But finds no treasure there.
Its victory is temporary,
Its happiness is thin;
The seeds it sows return at last
And show what grew within.

Open your eyes;
The morning is new.
Watch how the leaves
Unfurl into blue.
Each day brings wonder,
Each life makes a sign;
Nature keeps weaving
The world into life.

Honor your father,
Honor your mother,
Honor the teacher
Who opened the door.
The one is the many,
The many the whole;
Truth lives within us,
And shelters the soul.

Summer moonlight rests on leaves,
The midnight air is still;
The branches make a sheltering roof
Above the sleeping hill.
A quiet figure lies in grass,
With dew around her hair;
The night breathes softly through the trees,
And leaves its silver there.

One love has left, another ends;
The day goes down as well.
I know another heart may come,
But not the one I lost.
We thought our bond could bear the storm,
Could outlast pain and fear;
I was mistaken, and the room
Still keeps you standing here.

The trees have finished dressing,
Their branches bare and thin;
A moon of liquid silver moves
Through all the dark within.
They have prepared for winter,
They sleep beneath the cold;
The wise tree does not fear the snow—
It knows what spring will hold.

I am wealthy and empty,
I am humble and proud;
I am clever and foolish,
I am quiet and loud.
I toast with Mrs. Long,
I lie with Moll Kerr;
Whatever I claim to be,
The world finds me there.

My soul, remain a patient guest;
The play is not yet through.
Do not condemn the turning plot
Before the final view.
Each day invents another scene,
Each hour changes the part;
The ending may redeem the play
And teach the waiting heart.

There was a young frog on a log
Who stared at the birds in the fog;
He leapt from his seat,
Ran down the street,
And hid in a town underdog.

Pale traveler of the upper air,
Why wander without rest?
You climb beyond the watching earth,
Then turn toward every west.
The stars are born and change their forms,
The heavens never stay;
You search for one enduring joy
And find it slips away.

S eeking the hidden pattern,
C ollecting clues from stone,
I n every test and question,
E xploring what is known;
N aming the world through evidence,
C omparing, asking why,
E ach answer opens one more door
Beneath the patient sky.

The white curtain folds and falls;
She crosses through the light.
It trembles in her amber eyes,
Then steadies into night.
The lamps are small, the afternoon
Leans softly on the wall;
She dances once across my life,
And leaves me with it all.

A man may offer little more
Than sympathy and care;
A few kind words, a listening hand,
A quiet presence there.
Not every grief needs answers;
Some sorrows need a friend
Who sits beside the wounded heart
Until the ache can end.

The wheel of life moves slowly on;
We chase what we call more—
A larger house, a brighter screen,
A longer road to drive.
Yet some refuse to keep the score,
Some miss the years they had;
The wanting hand is never full,
The quiet heart is glad.

Green valleys, green fields,
Green forests rolling wide;
Green as shamrocks after rain,
Green hills on every side.
Old Ireland, emerald land,
Your color will not cease;
You carry in your weathered heart
A memory of peace.

We live by little mercies:
A door held open,
A hand returned,
A patient word.
These small bright acts
Keep ugliness from being
The only shape of us.

Childhood is a rare small fire,
Bright as a summer bun;
It hops like a rabbit through the grass,
It laughs before the race is run.
It tastes like honey, sounds like rain,
It startles like a spark;
Hold it gently while it lasts,
Then carry it through dark.

Be yourself beneath the cloud,
Even when no one asks;
Walk without a borrowed face,
Unfasten all the masks.
Close your eyes, breathe in the day,
Let the world pass by;
Happiness is sometimes just
The self that does not hide.

Health is the first gift lent to us,
Then kindness of the mind;
Wealth is third, and friends arrive
To make the journey kind.
No treasure keeps its value long
Without a body’s grace;
The richest life is one that leaves
Some welcome in its place.

Red poppies sway beside the vines,
Their paper petals bright;
They lean across the amber grain
Beneath the summer light.
The hills are full of scarlet flags,
The fields begin to shine;
A red wind moves across the gold
And makes the earth divine.

My son has crossed the roughest road
And met each hill with grace;
The weight that tried to bend him down
Could not erase his face.
Good luck, my child; may years ahead
Bring blessings to your door.
No mother’s prayer has traveled farther
Or loved you any more.

Together they make one woven life;
Together they rise and fall.
They sing, they sleep, they share the tears,
They answer every call.
When distance pulls their hands apart,
The world becomes less kind;
They write their song by meeting again,
And leave no one behind.

She drives away from every worry,
The sports car bright and fast;
The highway opens like a door,
The heavy hours pass.
No destination needs a name,
No one can tell her stay;
She lets the road carry the fear
Into the widening day.

Gangnam!
Bright shoes turn,
Shoulders burn,
Palms rise high,
Birds wheel by.
Palm trees bow,
The beach moves now,
Strangers join the beat,
Gangnam in the street!

Good food,
Warm food,
Food that helps us grow;
Honey gives a little gold,
Berries make us glow.
Brownies make a frown appear,
Butter makes us fly;
Choose the meal that keeps you well,
And keep your wisdom high.

Mispronounced morning,
Pink-gold dawn;
Eggs and coffee,
Silk put on.
Dreams move swaggering
Through the room;
No shower yet—
Keep the perfume.

Believe in the poet’s heart,
Or at least believe it beats;
It reaches out to welcome all,
Then gives them back their seats.
Its power is not command,
Its freedom is not rule;
Let every sovereign spirit stand
Within the poet’s school.

Let the sun shine every morning,
Warm the body, clear the soul;
Let it find the hidden places
Where the winter made us cold.
When it climbs the final hill,
Let its golden work be done;
Earth can rest beneath the light
That asks for nothing more.

Write me into the heart,
Ink me into the sky;
Dip the pen in midnight blue,
And let the old stars fly.
When the heavens break with rain,
When every comet falls,
Your name will still be on the page
That keeps my spirit whole.

A green carpet underfoot,
A rough road close beside;
One invites a careless fall,
One teaches us to stride.
Both have reasons, both have use,
Both belong to school;
The child learns by walking where
No single path is rule.

At night I wonder if love waits,
If dreams can cross the lake;
I picture swans upon the dark,
Their silver wakes awake.
Then morning finds the room unchanged,
The bed, the window, me;
The one I dreamed would come to shore
Has vanished with the sea.

The lazy god lies on the rock,
His limbs beneath the sun;
He calls for Echo, calls his flock,
And wonders where they’ve gone.
“What have you made?” the river asks.
Pan lifts a reed and grins:
“A song for every mortal ear—
The first note now begins.”

Young men explain their deepest thoughts
Upon a grain of rice;
They balance tricks on tiny pins
And call the balance wise.
But true profundity is quiet,
And never needs applause;
It waits where love has left the room,
And knows the reason why.

Why are there no tears in heaven?
Will fear become unknown?
You walked away before I could
Persuade you to stay home.
The road is narrow, worn, and old,
The choices dusty too;
If heaven has no tears at all,
I’ll save mine here for you.

How can I meet the face of God
When I still fall each day?
I begin with prayer at dawn,
Then lose the path by noon.
Yet love remakes the broken heart
With every rising sun;
The morning dew is not as pure
As what grace leaves undone.

Success is built from failures,
From days that will not bend;
The ones who keep returning
May be the ones who win.
Adversity can close a gate,
But effort finds the seam;
The patient hand that tries again
Can make a road from stone.

Some words are light as feathers,
They carry color through the air;
Some words are heavy trucks
That leave their darkness everywhere.
Light and dark make language,
An arc across the page;
Life is written in both inks,
At every human age.

I paint without a brush,
I color without red;
I find a lawn, a person, a joke,
And put them in my head.
Sci-fi, prose, and punning games,
A novel, stage, and rhyme—
If all these shapes become one voice,
Perhaps that voice is mine.

If trust were made of wood and stone,
My attic would be full;
You gave me pieces, word by word,
And made the structure whole.
Each time you say that you love me,
I build a nest above;
Your promises become the straw
That shelters us from weather.

Chicago, why do you keep changing?
You wear a different face each day.
Your streets contain a thousand lives,
Your lake reflects them all.
You hold the honest and the false,
The new, the old, the strange;
I ask you why you must become
What everyone expects.

Awake at last, I write and wait;
The mind goes down a road
Of promises and open gates,
Then slips into the ravine.
I catch what good I can from there,
Preserve the noise of youth;
The future has no map yet,
But hope can make a path.

There was a small girl with a curl,
The brightest and worst in the world;
When good, she was sweet,
When bad, hard to meet,
But always a wonderful girl.

Keep the ball low through the verse,
Let the small words roll;
Pass the meaning side to side,
Then shoot it toward the goal.
Night gives way to morning light,
The heavens open wide;
The poem wins when language learns
To move instead of hide.

In every way, you fill the room;
In every way, you shine.
Your smallest acts become a gift,
Your joy becomes mine.
You are not perfect, nor need be;
Your existence is enough.
The world grows full of happiness
Whenever you appear.

Life’s angel watched a child at play,
His hands full of the spring;
The flowers he gathered opened bright,
Then fell from everything.
He looked up, puzzled by the loss,
While pity filled her eyes;
She knew the loveliest growing things
Must learn to bloom and die.

Love is choosing one dear face
When all the world is wide;
Romance is finding every face
Has something to provide.
One keeps the heart’s direction true,
The other opens doors;
Both can be true, and both can live
Within the heart of love.

My love is like a scarlet rose;
Call, and she will sing.
Her voice travels on the breeze,
Then settles on my skin.
The flower carries sweetness,
And also carries pain;
The heart beats hardest where the thorn
Has left its little stain.

Do you know how to swim?
I do not ask if you are alive;
The world has taught you currents,
The body knows the dive.
I ask whether you can swim
Against what pulls you down;
If yes, I honor every stroke
That keeps you from the ground.

The frog began to croak in rain,
The monkey called, “Beware!”
She answered, “My father says
There’s danger everywhere.”
The hiss came fast, the lesson ended;
She learned too late to hide:
The warning was not empty noise,
But wisdom from the side.

My black pen is my princess;
I need them both to write.
They disappear when I reach out,
And vanish at the crucial time.
I search beneath the papers,
I find the cap, not ink;
The princess and the pen have fled
Before I have a thought.

Sing of men in striped pajamas,
Ready for the day;
Sing of dresses with deep pockets,
Where handkerchiefs can stay.
One outfit makes a gentleman,
One makes a child look grand;
Both are useful, both are strange,
When fashion takes command.

The faces of creation
Reflect the strength we name;
The trees, the animals, the human heart
Are not outside the frame.
No single truth is separate
From nature, earth, or man;
The world keeps showing us itself
In every living face.

It rains again in Detroit,
And Susan, I think it’s fair;
The streetlights blur, the sidewalks shine,
The wetness fills the air.
It is as pretty as your smile,
As bright as girls at play;
A hundred laughing faces pass,
And rain makes room for them.

Hope is the thing I wake with,
The first light in the room;
I hope for love, I hope for peace,
I hope the dark will bloom.
When plans go wrong, I hope again;
When all the roads are closed,
I hold a small unbroken wish
And let it lead me home.

In the folded rooms of thought
The truth waits without a name;
Justice raises broken dreams
And asks who caused the flame.
Let us look beyond the words,
Beyond the polished door;
The law can promise everything
And still protect the wrong.

Tea steams beside the window,
Noodles curl inside the bowl;
The afternoon is crowded,
But the breeze is soft and whole.
Friends arrive in twos and threes,
The cherry blossoms sway;
The cup is warm, the moment brief—
So take the day.

I do not prophesy each day;
The fire must first descend.
When spirit fills the waiting page,
The ordinary ends.
Then words go out like arrows,
Bright sparks across the world;
The flame grows cool, the ink grows still,
Until it comes again.

Do trees hear when we call out?
Does the dandelion feel
The hand that pulls it from the earth
And breaks its yellow wheel?
One day I am a blade of grass,
One day I am a name;
Life chooses what I am to be,
Then asks me to remain.

The powers gather reaching hands,
They claim what we possess;
They name the theft a public good,
Then leave us with less.
Soon they will own the hours we live,
The years we thought were ours;
The future waits behind a gate
Built out of borrowed power.

The child Krishna ran among the cows,
With laughter in the lane;
His friends followed through the dust,
His mother called again.
The divine wore a little boy’s face,
And mischief filled his eyes;
The village scolded, loved, and knew
The god in simple guise.

Faith is a hand in darkness,
Faith is the strength to stand;
Faith is believing in the self
And in a greater hand.
It is not proof that storms will cease,
Nor certainty of ease;
It is the choice to walk ahead
When doubt is on the breeze.

Higgledy-piggledy,
José Barroso,
Stiffly and starchedly,
Stood in the snow;
“No more plutonium,”
He cried to the sky,
Then climbed in a ship
And prepared to fly.

They said her words were balloons,
Too loose for my hands to hold;
Her love was a bargain in some shop,
Too cheap, too quickly sold.
But apples do not price the tree,
And rain does not explain;
The sun gives all its warmth away
Without accounting.

The day may press you toward the dark,
But darkness cannot stay;
Someone is waiting with a heart
That wants to light the way.
When yours grows small, it grows again;
When hope seems nearly gone,
Remember that I love you still,
And love keeps moving on.

Worry leaves by the open door,
The morning brings a bloom;
The road is rough, the wind is strong,
But friendship makes us room.
We sail through weather side by side,
We shelter one another;
The world is less impossible
When every friend is brother.

Wordsworth’s pastures stay forever green,
His summer skies stay blue;
He loved the fields of England,
And made their light renew.
The rhythm keeps the grasses bright,
The old lines still remain;
His poems build a country road
Through memory and rain.

Your every word is honey,
A tune from somewhere high;
It settles softly in my chest
And teaches pain to lie.
The sound moves toward the center,
Where hidden graces wait;
I hear your voice and find the world
More generous than fate.

When trouble comes, my family stays;
No door is shut to me.
They are the friends who know my face,
The shelter I can see.
They guard me through the difficult days,
They keep the lamps alight;
Whatever happens in the world,
They stand beside me still.

Somewhere in Paris, a café
Keeps one small table free;
The city sleeps beneath the stars,
The streets hold history.
The people wait for morning,
For change to cross the square;
Tonight the revolution is
Only a whisper there.

The waves return and strike the shore,
Then carry stones away;
They uncover tender clay
Beneath the hardened day.
A marmoset turns in the rain,
Its eyelids closing slow;
The storm keeps beating on the world,
And somewhere roots still grow.

Can God? God can!
Can God? God can!
The impossible opens
When faith begins.
Will God? God will!
Will God? God will!
The promise rises,
The promise is fulfilled.

Rose Aylmer, your remembered face
Still shines where candles fail;
The years have drawn a darker room,
But memory tells the tale.
The eyes that cannot see you now
Still weep beside the door;
I consecrate the quiet night
To what I loved before.

Stephen Wright was born by surgery,
Which caused him little pain;
But when he leaves his house, he finds
The doors are not the same.
He sometimes climbs out through a window,
For reasons strange and clear;
The world is full of exits
For a man who travels queerly.

Sirloin once filled my plate with pride;
Now coins are in my hand.
The meat has lost its former taste,
But soup can help me stand.
The bowl is hot, the broth is plain,
The future still moves on;
A meal need not be rich to give
The strength to meet the dawn.

To all who sleep far from the ones
They hoped would hold them near,
Remember that the world is wide
With others who know fear.
Some loneliness lasts one short night,
Some lasts a lifetime’s years;
No empty bed is empty alone—
The dark is full of tears.

Trust me with the pain you hide;
I will not make it mine.
Trust me with your guarded heart,
And I will give it time.
Trust me with the soul behind
The walls you built so high;
Let down one stone, then one more stone,
And let my love come by.

This food looks like a fallen shoe,
The soup smells like a drain;
The bread is old, the fries are cold,
The meat is half a flame.
I will not eat another bite,
My face has turned to blue;
If this is what the kitchen serves,
The kitchen serves it too.

Love hides beneath a friendly cloak,
Then laughs and shows its face;
It smiles through tears, it storms with rage,
Yet does not change its place.
The god may frown, the heavens shake,
The little heart may blame;
Whether it smiles or cries aloud,
Love is still the same.

I opened up the window wide
To drink the colors in;
But morning wore a veil of rain,
And would not let me in.
The sky was weeping over me,
The garden blurred from view;
I stood beside the dripping glass,
And found I wept there too.

I am alone inside the world,
And even tears stay dry;
No mother’s hand, no father’s voice,
No shoulder standing by.
I gather up the broken past,
I practice being new;
The lonely room is mine for now,
But I may make it through.

The moon rises round and bright,
The little stars withdraw;
Their scattered lights grow faint beneath
The silver that they saw.
The sky has room for only one
When night has found its face;
The stars step back, the moon moves on,
And fills the empty space.

Joy and joy—
Find it in the living,
Find it in the work;
Even when the day is hard,
Joy can still be found.
Look again, and look again;
Do not leave it where it lies.

Language begins as a simple hand,
Then grows a complicated cane;
An expert strikes a pattern out
And calls the rhythm plain.
The poet watches, heart in tears,
As rules reshape the art;
Yet every revolution starts
With language breaking open.

There was an Old Man of the Dee,
Who was bothered by one little flea;
He reached for a hatchet,
To cut it and catch it,
And frightened it straight up a tree.

The Good Shepherd came as a child,
In a manger, poor and bright;
The stars leaned close above the hay,
The world began anew that night.
The shepherds brought their wonder,
The lost were called by name;
Love entered through a stable door
And never left the same.

May life be so generous to you
That those who love you now
Will find their love grow deeper still
When later years arrive.
May every good thing you have done
Return in gentler form;
May even heaven look with joy
Upon the life you’ve made.

Love is a gem without an age,
It catches every light;
It does not lose its value
When the years become more white.
An oath can hold two lives together,
But tenderness is proof;
The finest marriage is the one
That keeps its wonder new.

Destiny has failed me twice,
Yet I chose the road again;
Pride came before the falling,
But I have learned to bend.
Let fate turn up its hidden card,
Let chance decide the side;
I may not win the hand I want,
But I will choose my life.

If hope has vanished overnight,
Or disappeared by day,
Does absence make it less a dream
That once had found a way?
The world we see may be a veil,
The truth a distant gleam;
What leaves the hand can still remain
Inside the mind’s own dream.

At the river’s edge I stand,
Where rapids pull and shine;
I dive beneath the guilt I carried,
And leave it to the current.
The water takes the heavy years,
The old shame loses hold;
I rise with river in my blood,
And thank the hand that called.

When sympathy arrives in words,
Or friends speak well of you,
The kindness feels like sunlight
Breaking through the blue.
Advice may come by email,
Or in a letter’s hand;
The best advice is still the one
That helps you understand.

White Christmas roses bloom,
Soft as candle flame;
Their petals brighten winter’s room,
Their fragrance has no name.
Beside the tree they seem to hold
The season’s quiet grace;
Pure flowers in the darkest month,
And light upon the face.

A paper lantern hangs forgotten
After rain canceled the party;
It swings upon its nylon thread
Above the darkened lawn.
Yellow jasmine scents the air,
The wet grass holds the night;
One sad bright thing still sways there,
Refusing to go dark.

Pithy, precise,
Dry and wise,
Sharp as a stone,
True on its own.
Eight little words
Can open a door;
Question the saying,
Then question some more.

You were the one I wished to hold
When I was young and sure;
If life should take you from my side,
My love will still endure.
Before you leave, remember this,
Before the door is through:
Whatever road the heavens choose,
I will still care for you.

I have imagined Chicago all my life:
The lake wind, the crowded train,
The streets alive with strangers,
The freedom to begin again.
I would forget tomorrow there,
Forget what came before;
I’d walk until the city’s pulse
Became my own once more.

I polish the false self I made,
Then watch its grains run down;
The hourglass keeps turning
Through every borrowed crown.
I reverse it, build it up,
I call the shape my soul;
At last I let the sand fall free,
And stand transparent, whole.

The snake had chosen one small frog,
The frog had chosen fight;
They struck, withdrew, then struck again,
And neither gained the bite.
The meal remained impossible,
The standoff would not end;
Two hungry creatures, face to face,
With no one left to win.

The trees bent down like angels
Along the morning road;
Their branches brushed my tired face,
Their leaves received my load.
I wanted to dissolve into
The autumn mist and air,
To become the peace I saw there,
And leave behind despair.

The village drums begin at dusk;
The dancers cross the square.
They speak in voices shaped by home,
And lift their hands in air.
The festival becomes a song,
The language becomes flame;
Culture is the living room
Where generations meet.

Across my bed the moonbeams fall,
A cold and shining trail;
They look like frost upon a dream,
Too delicate to hold.
I raise my head and see the moon,
Then lower it once more;
I dream of home, my fatherland,
And all I knew before.

I love the rainbow’s many greens,
Its blue and yellow fire;
It tells the sky a secret truth
And lifts the heart up higher.
The colors shine, the colors fade,
The daylight moves along;
Still every arc above the rain
Feels like the world’s bright song.

At the doorway of beginning,
I watch you climb the stair;
I almost reach to hold you,
But someone calls you back.
You turn, I smile, the moment breaks,
And tears fall where you stood;
Some meetings last a lifetime,
Some only teach us hope.

In times like these, let silence speak;
The poet cannot mend the state.
No verse can make a ruler wise,
No rhyme can close a gate.
The world has heard enough advice
From mouths that love applause;
Sometimes the most honest poem
Is quiet without cause.

The world is an inn,
And I am passing through;
I eat what nature places out,
Then pay the bill in time.
The hostess gives what she can spare,
The room is mine awhile;
I rest, I rise, I leave the key,
And travel on the road.

I marched beneath a borrowed call,
Promised a world made new;
Sixteen days of shining words,
And then what will we do?
The crowd awaits the trumpets,
The leader takes the stage;
We stand beneath the rising sun,
And wonder at the age.

Was that a sign?
Or only light?
Did your eyes ask me to stay,
Or pity what I might become?
My mind divides itself in two;
I guess, I wait, I doubt.
Make your move before the silence
Makes the answer out.

Happiness has no shoreline;
You cannot hold its hue.
It has no scent, no shape to touch,
Yet it can carry you.
The mind may raise it, mind may break it,
Like weather in the air;
We search for joy as though it waits,
Then find it everywhere.

How strange to ask love to live inside
The walls of any room;
It fills the heart, it rules the mind,
It makes its own wide home.
The one who tries to hold it close
May find it cannot stay;
Love needs a sky above its head,
And space to choose its way.

Christmas lights are on the streets,
The town has found its cheer;
Walk beneath the shining trees,
The holiday is here.
No gift is needed for a smile,
No purse must overflow;
Be merry with the people near,
And let the bright days glow.

When hope arrives, tranquility
Becomes a living thing;
It circles over tired brows
On quiet, patient wings.
The worker lifts his head again,
The heavy air grows mild;
Peace is not an empty room,
But labor reconciled.

Around the ocean, mountain, plain,
The earth changes its design;
The desert keeps a yellow hush,
The fertile fields make green lines.
I gather every panorama,
The near, the far, the strange;
The world unfolds its many faces
Whenever I arrange it.

There are ghosts inside my engine;
They rattle when I drive.
One whispers from the dashboard,
One shivers near the wheel.
I stop beside the roadside,
The silence answers back;
Perhaps the ghosts are only parts
That need a little care.

Life bumps us from the road,
Then kicks us from behind;
We stand up, brush the dust away,
And laugh at what we find.
The gift of humor keeps us young,
It turns the bruise to gold;
The world may make us older,
But laughter makes us whole.

Where are the butterflies going?
Their flight has lost a line;
The breeze turns them from side to side,
The sky erases signs.
They have no armor, no defense,
No map to guide the wing;
Yet thousands of their fragile beats
Can change a distant spring.

Like a turtle, I carry art
Wherever I must go;
It is not weight upon my back,
It is the home I know.
The shell protects the faithful work,
The road becomes its room;
What others call a burden
Is the place where I can bloom.

The yellow pen marks every page,
But you use it to write;
The black and blue are waiting there,
For letters clear and right.
Do not turn the tools around,
Do not confuse their roles;
Every color has a task
In making language whole.

Cloud-pale eyes, asleep with dreams,
Outshine the poet’s art;
No perfect line can rival them,
No crafted rhyme the heart.
The stars remain unlabored,
The woman needs no song;
I bow before the beauty that
Was beautiful all along.

The buffet waits untouched;
The white-shirted servers stand.
The food has made its offering,
Though no one takes a hand.
A poet drinks his tea alone,
And fills a page instead;
The feast remains, the words begin,
The table turns to sacrament.

Whether the weather is warm,
Whether the weather is cold,
Whether the rain strikes the roof,
Whether the wind takes hold,
We will weather the weather,
Whatever the weather may say;
The world can change its weather,
But not our choice to stay.

Dance before Nataraja,
Dance beneath the watching gods;
Dance for knowledge, dance for light,
Dance upon the ancient roads.
Dance for goodness, dance for joy,
Dance for the hidden flame;
The spirit moves through every limb,
And movement speaks its name.

“Where shall we live?” the wanderers ask.
The winds reply, “Look high.”
No roof is nobler than the blue,
No ceiling like the sky.
Beneath that dome we join our lives,
Beneath its watch we stand;
The world becomes a home enough
When heaven holds the land.

Some classes drag like winter rain,
But do not fall asleep;
Finish all the homework first,
Then let the evening leap.
Go out, laugh, and play awhile,
Return before the bell;
The clever student studies hard,
Then knows when to relax.

Anagram, gram, rag, and ram,
The letters turn and sing;
Emotion, beauty, wit, and hope
Are hidden in the ring.
One special person enters,
And every sound grows sweet;
The alphabet becomes a garden
Where two hearts meet.

Be careful who you hand your work to;
Choose the critic well.
Tell the story nearly whole,
But keep one room to yourself.
Then bend your ear toward the soul,
Where the truest answer waits;
The loudest voice is not always
The one that understands.

As far away as the blue horizon,
The past still holds its place;
The hills remember what we were,
The stones retain our names.
You and I are distant now,
But memory keeps the view;
The world can change its shape and still
Leave yesterday in blue.

A child should tell the honest truth,
And answer when addressed;
At table, use a quiet voice,
And try to do your best.
No child is perfect every day,
But manners make a start;
The smallest acts of courtesy
Can grow a generous heart.

There was an Old Man of Dundee,
Who climbed to the top of a tree;
When the crows made a fuss,
He shouted, “I’ll rush
Straight home to Dundee for my tea!”

Milo quotes the sacred page
To prove how wise he is;
He pays his soul to win the name,
And calls the bargain bliss.
It is a pity wit should cost
The part that makes us whole;
The cleverest crown is empty
When it covers no soul.

If I could read your hidden heart,
I might forgive the lies;
But trust once cracked will never make
The same unbroken shape.
I thought we’d reach the final door,
I thought the vow was true;
Now every public victory
Reminds me what I knew.

The rose rose up through concrete,
Where no soft garden grew;
It found a crack, it found the sun,
It found its way through.
The city said the law was fixed,
The flower disagreed;
It kept its dream, and learned to breathe
Where no one planted seed.

No one sees the lonely eyes;
They hide behind the grin.
The strongest faces carry tears
That never reach the skin.
At night, when every witness leaves,
The hidden sorrow starts;
Goodbyes and friendless afternoons
Lie deep inside those eyes.

Small joys line my ordinary life:
A flower standing in the wind,
A little light across the floor,
A future waiting just beyond.
Today is full of shadows still,
But tomorrow has a door;
I wait inside the present
For what it may become.

I am the past, asking questions;
You are the one who must reply.
Imagine answers that are true
For the world you built and live in.
Do not borrow another person’s road,
Or wear another person’s sky;
The future asks what you will make
Of what I left behind.

Indestructible Maureen,
You are anything but quiet;
When your voice crosses Billingham,
The distant hills grow bright.
Roseberry hears you calling,
The walkers stop to grin;
No one can mistake the sound
Of Maureen arriving.

Bend low, summer stars;
You seem near enough to take.
The sky is a dark bowl,
The constellations shake.
I reach, but they move farther;
I hum beneath the dome.
The stars are not a ceiling—
They are the road back home.

Words spoken in the mind
Can travel farther than the voice;
They cross the dark toward grace,
Though no ear hears the choice.
Some bond remains between the soul
And what it cannot see;
The conversation continues
When all else falls away.

Kunti, mother of the Pandavas,
Held sorrow in her hands;
She raised the princes through the storms
That shook their ancient lands.
One son she left, one son she loved,
And paid for that divide;
Her tears became a hidden river
Running at her side.

You may fear the passing stranger,
And rightly guard the door;
But kin who make the household cold
Can wound you even more.
If those who share your name were kind,
The world would lose its threat;
No stranger’s clever trap could match
The harm of home’s neglect.

Sister, you are treasure,
The steady hand I know;
You lift me when the world turns gray,
You help my courage grow.
No language holds the place you keep,
No gift could take it through;
The heart has one enduring room,
And I have saved it for you.

You have honored the work of years,
The people who believed;
You carried every challenge through,
You earned what you achieved.
Hold your head high; the goal is here,
The road has made you strong;
The future waits beyond the gate,
And you have waited long.

A frog watched a bird in the sky,
And wished that he too could fly;
“I’m almost a bird,”
The proud frog declared,
While fish in the stream laughed nearby.

You appear like a reflection
In a mirror filled with mist;
One strong breath might scatter you,
One touch might make you shift.
Yet you are not a dream I keep,
Or only memory’s art;
I reach into the hazy air,
And find you in my heart.

Have you heard the giraffe laugh?
Have you heard the chimpanzee?
The rhino tells a heavy joke,
The flea giggles with glee.
The jungle keeps its humor
In every size and sound;
Even the quietest little laugh
Can turn the world around.

White surf rises, bows, and runs
Back into the sea;
It returns to greet the shore,
Again and endlessly.
We huddle close and laugh aloud,
The water at our feet;
The ocean keeps its old refrain,
And makes the moment sweet.

Dew rests lightly in Julia’s hair,
Small stars along the strand;
The morning has been generous,
The stream reflects the light.
Each droplet trembles as she moves,
Then falls before my eyes;
The day keeps making little moons
Wherever she goes by.

I work through Dumas père,
I work through Dumas fils;
The pages fill my waking hours,
But neither moves my heart.
The names are grand, the sentences,
The heroes rise and fall;
Yet scholarship cannot command
The feeling to arrive.

Cupid, take my heart home;
I am content tonight.
Give me a hammock, someone close,
And conversation’s light.
Let darkness gather round us slow,
Let no one interrupt;
The world can wait beyond the trees—
For now, this love is enough.

The heart loves love beyond the mind,
Beyond the clock’s control;
Time plays with every tender thing,
But cannot end the soul.
Love circles through the hours we lose,
It outlives every part;
The mind may tire, the years may close,
But love keeps time within the heart.

Something is wrong with all of them—
The weather men adore the heat.
They speak of sun as though it heals,
While I dream of snow and sleet.
Give me a blizzard through the glass,
Give me a sky gone white;
I am a winter-hearted soul
In every summer forecast.

I walk the empty beach alone,
The damp sand cool and close;
The breeze moves gently up my arms,
The restless water rolls.
My thoughts unwind like long wet ropes,
The horizon makes them new;
The quiet shore asks nothing back,
And leaves me breathing clear.

Thinking of God makes gladness grow;
A poem opens the heart.
A picture, a hopeful thought,
Can give the day a start.
The mind can help the body heal,
The spirit can stand strong;
Faith is the hand beneath the step
That helps us move along.

The marriage cart needs two strong hands,
Two shoulders at the wheel;
One person cannot carry it
Through every turning hill.
If wife and husband pull as one,
The road becomes more kind;
If either leaves the other alone,
The cart will lose its way.

The birds have left the mountain;
One cloud drifts through the blue.
The mountain and I remain,
With nothing else to do.
We watch each other quietly,
The stone, the sky, and me;
The world can empty out its noise,
And still the view is whole.

What dream are you still sleeping through,
You modern dreamer, wake!
Rise and draw the map yourself,
For no one else can make it.
Give the morning what you have,
Let the hidden colors show;
The dream becomes a shining road
The moment that you go.

You complete me with a mark,
You dot the letters clean;
You cross my t and question me,
Then make my meaning seen.
I copy all your secret signs,
I rearrange the phrase;
Perhaps the plan was love all along,
Disguised as grammar’s maze.

The greatest teacher is the one
Who walks with us through fear;
The kindest hand, the gentlest voice,
The one who stays near.
I call that teacher Jesus Christ,
Whose love outlasts the years;
He teaches through a quiet life,
Through mercy, not commands.

When a king disliked a courtier,
He gave him a white elephant;
To care for such a holy beast
Would spend the man’s last cent.
To neglect the gift was dangerous,
To keep it meant despair;
The finest present in the world
Can be a hidden snare.

The firework cracks above the town,
The people leave their doors;
Red fountains bloom against the sky,
Gold thunder shakes the floors.
The children stare, the parents smile,
The night becomes a bed;
At dawn the smoke is still there,
And every spark has fled.

His turtleneck hides his flea collar;
His package is a mess.
He thinks himself a secret star,
But no one is impressed.
If he could start his life again,
He’d still choose self-regard;
The neatest way to wrap a fool
Is in a tangled heart.

Close your eyes—the sun is there,
Massaging the dark;
The moon becomes a silver plate
That catches every spark.
The light exposes hidden things,
The night receives the rest;
Between the two, the dreaming mind
Finds what it loves best.

I cannot stop looking at your face;
It burns from somewhere deep.
Your beauty is not merely skin,
But waters I can drink.
I see a lake of gathered thought,
Fresh wisdom in its flow;
I want to enter all that blue,
And never let it go.

Love, love, love—
A warm and wandering flame;
It rises from the hidden heart,
Then calls another name.
We give it to the cherished ones,
We keep it when we grieve;
The world is changed by what we share,
And what we still believe.

A single star beside the moon
Can make the whole sky bright;
It flickers like a little lamp
That learned to hold the night.
I feel enormous under it,
Yet small enough to see;
The star is far, the star is one,
And still it speaks to me.

I was a daughter first,
Then someone’s beloved wife;
I built a house, became a mother,
And filled it with a life.
The names I carry fit me well,
Yet one question will not cease:
Which self beneath the many names
Is the one that belongs to me?

Dactyl knows me, anapest too;
Iamb will tap my door.
Why wait for human praise to come
When rhythm offers more?
The meter is my company,
The cadence is my friend;
I’ll take my poems to the judge
Whose hearing has no end.

I am blessed to have your love,
Though distance makes it ache;
I know your face, but cannot touch
The warmth your hands would make.
The heart can hold what arms cannot,
Can keep a voice nearby;
I love you through the empty space,
And ask the world why.

Each ripple is not a wave,
Each wave may miss the shore;
Still water keeps on traveling,
And asks us to make more.
Our efforts spread beyond our sight,
Some reach the edge at last;
Success is often one small ring
That grew from all the rest.

When destiny comes walking near,
I yield the reins at last;
My shape becomes a piece of clay
In hands beyond my grasp.
The future molds what I become,
The present learns to wait;
I do not know the sculptor’s plan,
But trust the turning fate.

Morning breaks through colored glass,
And floods the room with light;
The past lies pale behind the pane,
The future gathers bright.
I open every shutter wide,
I let the new day in;
At the end of every rainbow,
Another road begins.

Imagination has no edge;
It climbs beyond the hill.
It pours blue rivers through the sky,
Makes empty shapes move still.
It gives the mind a thousand doors,
It turns a thought to art;
The colors that it wakes in us
Can astonish the heart.

Sometimes you laugh,
Sometimes you cry,
Sometimes the reason passes by.
Sometimes you shine,
Sometimes you fall;
Sometimes no feeling speaks at all.
You come, you leave, you change your view,
But every form is still you.

There was an Old Man with a beard,
Who thought that his breakfast was weird;
Two owls and a hen,
Four larks and a wren,
Had nested there all through the year.

So little is offered at the chapel,
While so much is spent at the game;
The nation calls itself wealthy,
Then forgets the poor by name.
If history records our grandeur,
Let it tell the whole of the score:
Not what we spent to entertain,
But what we gave to the poor.

Money, money—give me more;
The appetite has no end.
While one hand gathers every coin,
Another cannot spend.
The thirst for wealth can drain the well
And leave the needy dry;
No fortune lasts forever,
No purse can buy the sky.

SNAKE
Cold, coiled, silent,
Sliding through the grass,
Fangs hold a hidden warning,
Reptile.

FISH
Bright, quick, silver,
Turning through the stream,
Water carries every dream,
Aquatic.

Politicians fear the difficult choice;
They trade their moral courage for a share.
Each wants a piece of the public cake,
But those who truly make the sacrifice
Rarely remain inside the halls of power.

Far out at sea, I sailed through memory,
My little boat concealed by years;
The mist became an anecdote,
The storm became a song.
I found the turns that shaped my life,
I sang against the rain;
The waves did not erase the past,
But taught me how to steer.

Moon-charms, work your quiet spell;
Ease the fevered mind to sleep.
Gather pain in silver threads,
Lower it into dreams.
Let the weary body rest,
Let the broken senses heal;
When morning opens its blue eyes,
Let peace be what is real.

My aim is tomorrow,
My need is the road;
My future is waiting
To carry its load.
The goal becomes distance,
The distance becomes near;
I walk toward the life I want,
And make the path appear.

Without the heroine,
What play can call itself romance?
She enters with her painted face,
And gives the plot its chance.
Her costume, voice, and secret smile
Complete the world we see;
Remove her from the stage, and love
Loses its mystery.

Newborn child, bright gift of love,
May angels guard your sleep;
May every road you travel on
Be gentle, wide, and deep.
The world is waiting for your steps,
The morning for your eyes;
May grace remain beside your path
From cradle to the skies.

I crossed the world to find some joy,
And spent my trust and time;
I reached a kingdom made of dust,
Where every gate was closed.
Then, when the search had emptied me,
I turned toward the Lord;
The thing I sought in distant lands
Was waiting in His word.

A boat full of fish is a lucky wish;
One fish upon the line
Is supper waiting on the dish,
And proof that patience shines.
The sea may keep its larger wealth,
The hook may miss its goal;
One silver catch can feed a house
And satisfy the soul.

Aeronaut, your bubble rose
Above the grass and gravel;
Then one woman’s watching eyes
Brought you back to earth.
No more free flight above the field,
No more unbounded travel;
She drew a line, and from that day
You walked where she would lead.

In the driest desert,
Under the patient stars,
You and I shared ancient thoughts,
Turning pages in the dark.
We could have stayed forever there,
Beneath the open dome;
The sand would keep our footprints,
The sky would be our home.

Faith has no feet,
Yet it goes on;
Faith has no wings,
Yet it can fly.
It rests in the heart,
It grows through allegiance,
Then breaks into light
As hope and confidence.

There are two worlds inside the heart:
The world of what I am,
The world of what my hands have done,
The record of my days.
But beneath the flower, fruit, and root,
One living truth remains:
The world of love is where the life
Of every other grows.

Rearranging blue,
The bowerbird works;
Shiny words and feathers,
His little magic world.
The pantoum turns around him,
The pattern will not end;
He is always building beauty,
And never has the time.

Words can cut like hidden glass,
Or bend the soul awry;
Words can sound like hammered iron,
Or lift a heart to fly.
The voice decides the shape they take,
The listener feels the art;
Love turns language into joy,
And cruelty into scars.

The boy chased a butterfly
Through the lady’s garden wall;
He caught the wings, he laughed aloud,
Then watched their colors fall.
The prize he wanted in his hand
Was ruined by the grasp;
Some beauty can be kept alive
Only when it is free.

Mark the day with music;
A child has entered earth.
May grace surround her growing years,
May wisdom know her worth.
Give her a mother’s gentleness,
A father’s patient art;
Add learning, laughter, courage, too,
And shelter for her heart.

I woke inside a second dream,
And still had not arrived;
The music of the road below
Had somehow come alive.
Rock-and-roll heaven found the earth,
The streets began to sing;
I had not gone beyond the world—
The world had grown its wings.

You told me poems must walk in meter,
Five beats marching line by line;
Yet every day you search for mine,
As though the rule were not divine.
You say you will not read a verse
Unless its feet are measured right,
But miss the restless little poems
That keep you awake at night.

Mirror, tell me what is beautiful:
The face, the thought, the deed?
Should truth be spoken without care,
Or hidden when we bleed?
Can morality be weighed and sold
For dollars, pounds, or pence?
If someone strikes without a cause,
Must patience make no sense?

Life is a chapter made of lessons,
Some narrow, some immense;
The dawn begins the opening line,
The years supply the text.
The questions grow more difficult,
The answers change their shape;
We learn the book by turning pages,
And never see the end.

Big George put springs inside his shoes,
And suddenly could fly;
He bounced beyond the finish line,
He nearly touched the sky.
Fourteen extra rounds he ran,
While everyone looked on;
The clever gadget made him fast,
But not for very long.

Russet leaves and amber leaves
Lie thick along the lane;
The autumn wears a jeweled crown
Before it turns to rain.
The final burst of color burns
Across the country floor;
The season gives its richest gift,
Then gives a little more.

The angel who attended birth
Told the child, “Go and love;
You need no other earthly tool,
No blessing from above.”
The child stepped into joy and light,
The world became a part;
The angel knew that love alone
Could teach the growing heart.

Once they named us by a country;
Then by another name.
We speak through weather, flags, and doubt,
And ask what makes us one.
Are we courageous? Are we true?
Can we stand the rain?
Do we share the same red cross,
Or only different socks?

The prodigal son has come back home;
The door is open wide.
He calls to say he’s on his way,
And old tears turn to pride.
At last he is prepared to return,
At last he says the words:
“I love you.”
Nothing else is needed.

I woke from a dream inside a dream,
And found the music here;
Rock-and-roll heaven had come down
To fill the earthly air.
The streets became a stage of light,
The night began to sing;
I had not traveled anywhere—
The world had grown its wings.

I think no billboard can compare
With one green living tree;
The signs may cover every wall,
But roots are what I see.
If all the advertisements fall,
The branches will remain;
The tree will hold the open sky
Above the town again.

Our seaside camp had painted sails,
And buckets lined the shore;
We counted shells and skipped flat stones,
Then counted them once more.
The afternoon grew long and still,
The gulls flew out of sight;
The tide withdrew beyond the bay
And did not come that night.

I wish, I wish,
You would arrive,
You would arrive and stay with me,
Not merely pass me by.
I wish, I wish,
My work would bloom,
Though I envy no one else,
And keep my spirit calm.
I wish, I wish,
Your kindness reached
The lonely room where I have been
Learning how to smile.
I wish, I wish, for quiet joy,
For peace enough to breathe.

Have you ever held regret?
I think it tastes like salt;
It stings the tongue, then fades away,
Though we insist it’s faultless.
If every feeling had a flavor,
Regret would start as brine,
Then turn to rain upon the lips
And leave a trace behind.
Regret tastes faintly of the sea,
Regret tastes faintly of time.

spin spin spin
come close for
an evening grin
begin begin begin
catch the beat
and let the room begin
spin spin spin
let the bright
old record pull you in
swing with me now
stay with me now
come on, darling,
let’s begin

Take my hand.
There is a road
beyond the quarrel
of the page.
Let other voices
keep their careful
rooms of silence,
keeping every
word behind a door.
For me,
Take my hand.
We can walk where
language ends.

When I am tired
Of counting every loss,
When evening settles
Cold against the glass,
When I say your name
To someone who remembers,
I know the old ache
Would open like a window
If I could find you
Under the boardwalk lights,
Or watch you pin your hair
Before you leave the room.

Can any master teach the seed
The shape of its appointed tree?
The child we hope will save the day
Must learn from more than books can say.
He needs the trembling of the reed,
The patience of a winter field,
The sudden courage of the sky
When morning makes the dark retreat.
Then, rooted in his inward ground,
He will gather the ages round
And give tomorrow a new name.

Praise to you who keep the key
To rooms of bright discovery!
Hail, you daughters nine of song,
Who make the quiet hours belong.
Teach my clumsy hands to find
A melody within the mind;
Let every line I offer rise
Like laurel green beneath the skies.
If my small hymn should ever last,
Crown it with leaves that will not pass.

Believe in me,
Says the voice above.
I shaped the rivers,
I named the stars,
And every living thing
Is carried in my keeping.
You are not abandoned,
Though the night is wide.

The dawn split open through the clouds
And pulled her from her sleep.
Her head was heavy as a stone,
Her hands were rough with work.
A harsh command rang through the house;
The old floor shook with feet.
She rose beside the kitchen fire,
And met the day once more.
They called her patient, called her kind—
But no one saw the crown
She wore beneath the ash and dust,
Or heard her dreaming sound.

I love the heat of a winter stove,
I love the rain on my face;
I love the light in a stranger’s room,
And leaving without disgrace.
I love a door that opens wide,
A road that asks me through;
The world is kindest at its edge,
Where nothing says, “Stay true.”

The rain arrived without a word,
As sudden as a sneeze.
I should have brought my yellow coat,
I should have checked the trees.
My collar’s wet, my socks are wet,
My pockets hold a stream;
I once was caught beneath a hose,
But this has more ambition!

Hush—the valley holds its breath,
And distant fields turn white.
See! A silver seam of weather
Climbs the edge of night.
Shut the gate. The air is warm;
The chimney smoke bends low.
Look—the storm has found our road
And will not let us go.
Come beneath the cedar’s bough;
Quick, before you stumble...
There! The first hard flakes have struck.
Hear the north wind grumble.

Who I become is not a stone
Placed in my hand at birth.
It is the road I choose to walk,
The work I judge of worth.
It is the ember kept alive
When every torch is gone;
Not merely where the fire has been,
But what it warms at dawn.
A name may point toward who I was;
My choices write who I become.

I like a word that answers back:
A yes means open door.
A no means turn around and find
A different path to explore.
But “perhaps” hangs in the air,
And “we’ll see” leaves me blue.
“Tomorrow” has a little hope;
“Later” has a view.
Still, when someone says “not yet,”
I know the clock is moving.

I am wearing a bathing suit,
And the river holds my knees.
There is water under water here,
So do not fear the deep.
You, too, were shaped by rain and tide;
Come closer to the blue.
We may remain from year to year,
As floating shadows do.
Who is the finest swimmer?
I could tell you, but I won’t.
My poems learn the river’s shape;
You are the shore they want.

One wore a shining ribbon,
And two possessed a smile,
But ribbons, smiles, and clever eyes
Could not persuade the hill.
The grass remembered every foot,
The stone remembered rain;
Only the hollow left behind
Showed where the hare had lain.

At sunset, little shadows creep
Across the bedroom wall;
Some wear the shape of crooked hands,
Some climb and some grow tall.
One twists itself into a vine,
One scurries like a mouse,
But every shadow follows me
Around the quiet house.

Drums roll beneath the stadium lights,
The marching band turns bright;
Flags rise and fall above the field,
And every seat is white.
The players gather at the line,
Their helmets catch the glow;
A roar travels from end to end
Before the whistle blows.
Two teams charge into the night,
And Saturday takes flight.

THAT smile conceals a crooked thought,
I cannot call it fair;
His eyes announce an honest man,
But mischief lingers there.
He swears his master means no harm—
The evidence says why:
A polished tongue may hide a thief,
But not from every eye.

Stop looking outward for the truth.
Sit quietly and listen.
Before you question every voice,
Ask what your own has hidden.
How much of what you call your life
Is story dressed as fact?
And when you say, “I know myself,”
What makes you sure of that?

sometimes my friend
I shut my eyes to find
an undiscovered room
behind the doors of mind
then I open them and see
what brightness made me blind
there are familiar streets I pass
without perceiving them
and every day the world reveals
what I had missed again

I am a man;
I ask for kindness,
A little patience,
A little warmth.
I do not need
A grand procession,
Nor riches poured
Into my arms.
Give me a sentence
Spoken gently.
Give me a hand
That does not leave.

Blessed is the one
who wakes and can still say:
This morning belongs to me;
I will not trade it away.
Let tomorrow bring its thunder,
Let yesterday keep its claim.
The living heart has only now,
And now is not a shame.
He who has used this single day
Has not lived it in vain.

the teacher speaks
and thinks my eyes are fixed
my teacher is a patient guide
my teacher makes me sick
my teacher is my father
my teacher is the bell
